item.title: 4 players Broncos should target before NFL trade deadline
item.description: The NFL trade deadline is looming and trade rumors around the league are heating up. Which teams will be buyers and which teams will be sellers? There have already been some big trades, as the Indianapolis Colts have moved both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and more recently, the Tennessee Titans shipped defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for three draft picks, including two first-rounders. The Denver Broncos should be thinking squarely about being a potential buyer to help bolster their Super Bowl hopes, and there are some players out there who could be available. While there are some players on the roster the Broncos should consider trading away due to the fact that they will soon hit free agency, these four players should be in their sights before the Nov.10 trade deadline officially hits. 4 players Broncos should target before NFL trade deadline 1. Jonathan Taylor, RB, Indianapolis Colts This is going to be the most popular name on here as the Colts seem to be in fire-sale mode after moving Nelson and Buckner. Speculation about where Jonathan Taylor, one of the best running backs in the league, could end up has been running rampant. However, Taylor has stated he is proud to be with the Colts and isn't looking to be traded. That doesn't mean it won't happen. The Colts are clearly in full rebuild mode, and if the right offer comes along, they could take it. The Broncos have been connected to the rumors surrounding Taylor and the idea of adding him does make sense as the Broncos need to find more success in the running game. Don't look for George Paton and Sean Payton to make this move, as it's much more likely that they are happy with what Jonah Coleman brings to the team, and fitting Taylor's contract into the salary cap could be tricky. 2. Saquon Barkley, RB, Philadelphia Eagles The Philadelphia Eagles came into this season as contenders, but after a 2-5 start to the season while seeing their starting quarterback, Jalen Hurts, have his season cut short over a blood clot issue, they could suddenly be sellers. There has been talk of the Broncos looking at the Eagles' all-world running back, Saquon Barkley, who might be the most exciting name on this list. Barkley has had some injury issues throughout his career, but he's a complete running back who is as good as anyone at the position. It would be interesting to see what he could cost if the Eagles are even interested in trading him, but it's certainly worth a phone call from Paton to Howie Roseman to find out. 3. The Broncos have been connected to trading for Saints running back Alvin Kamara since Sean Payton became the head coach, and it's somewhat surprising that it hasn't happened. item.title: Greg Olsen reportedly seen as favorite to replace Troy Aikman at ESPN despite brief history with network brass
item.description: Credit: MARK ZALESKI / THE TENNESSEAN If Troy Aikman leaves ESPN after this season, much of the industry already has a pretty good idea of who will sit next to Joe Buck. The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand reported that Fox’s Greg Olsen is widely considered within sports media circles to be the frontrunner to replace Aikman on Monday Night Football. ESPN could also try to lure Peyton or Eli Manning , Travis or Jason Kelce , according to Marchand, or dangle the possibility of an NFL role to Kirk Herbstreit , though Herbstreit just signed a new deal to remain on Prime Video’s Thursday Night Football . Olsen spent two seasons as Fox’s lead analyst alongside Kevin Burkhardt , calling Super Bowl LVII and winning a Sports Emmy just before Tom Brady’s $375 million contract relegated him to the network’s No. 2 booth with Joe Davis , where he has since beaten out Brady for another Emmy . He has never concealed his desire to reclaim a top seat , and Puck’s John Ourand reported in August that Olsen’s Fox contract, which expires after this season , includes a clause allowing him to leave for a lead analyst job elsewhere. Fox has yet to open negotiations on an extension, per Richard Deitsch , and with CBS recently locking up J.J. Watt as its permanent lead analyst , ESPN’s Monday Night Football chair may be the only top booth realistically available to Olsen this offseason. Olsen’s relationship with ESPN’s top brass is minimal, however. According to Marchand, he has met chairman Jimmy Pitaro and content president Burke Magnus only once, and briefly. At last season’s College Football Playoff national championship between Olsen’s alma mater, Miami, and Buck’s alma mater, Indiana, Olsen stopped by ESPN’s luxury suite at halftime to visit former Bears teammate Dusty Dvoracek, now an ESPN college football analyst , and shook hands with Pitaro and Magnus on his way through. Marchand reported that Buck left Fox in 2022 partly because he was reluctant to break in a then-inexperienced Olsen and doubted Fox would land Brady, repeatedly insisting he wanted to keep working with Aikman. Four years later, Puck’s Dylan Byers reported last week that Buck would welcome Olsen as his next partner , part of an extension process that left Aikman feeling betrayed and contributed to the pair’s SoFi Stadium blowup earlier this month, which Marchand detailed this week , revealing that Aikman met privately with Pitaro beforehand and accused Buck of betraying him once the argument began. Aikman has since put the odds of returning to television next season at 50/50, and with his contract expiring in March , ESPN appears increasingly likely to need a new analyst before its next Monday Night Football season begins. If that analyst does turn out to be Olsen, Buck will finally get around to breaking in the partner he once left Fox to avoid. item.title: Penn State vs. Purdue: Three Keys to Victory
item.description: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Tony Siracusa, CFB Managing Editor Penn State returns to Beaver Stadium Saturday to host 3-4 Purdue. Will this be the Nittany Lions’ first Big Ten win of the season, or will the Boilermakers snap a 22-year-long losing streak against the blue and white? If Penn State hopes to turn the four-game losing streak into an 8-4 season, the former must happen. Here are a few ways that the Nittany Lions can get that first conference win of 2026. Penn State vs. Purdue: Three Keys to Victory Must Limit Turnovers Turnovers are backbreakers, obviously, but that was exemplified in the 21-18 loss to Michigan before the bye week. Quarterback Rocco Becht threw two interceptions and fumbled once in the second half against the Wolverines, and all three turnovers turned into touchdown drives. Michigan’s offense only scored following a Becht turnover. Penn State has not been a turnover-prone offense this season, now having a +4 turnover margin, but this can’t be an issue that persists. Especially by the fifth-year quarterback. Purdue has forced 10 turnovers in 2026, which ranks 42nd nationally. Don’t Let Purdue Reach the Red Zone The Boilermakers boast one of the best red zone offenses, ranking 11th nationally by scoring on 94.1% of red zone drives. Purdue has 32 red zone trips with 21 touchdowns and 11 field goals. Purdue running back Fame Ijeboi has nine rushing touchdowns this season. All of his scores have come from the red zone, with seven coming from inside the 3-yard line. Photo courtesy: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images While Penn State allows 18.9 points per game, its red zone defense ranks among the worst in the country at 126th, allowing a score on 95% of opponent red zone trips. Penn State has allowed 13 touchdowns and six field goals from the red zone on 20 attempts. However, the best way to stop a high-scoring red zone team is to not let them reach the red zone at all. The key will be forcing the Boilermakers to stay outside of the 20-yard line. Jacobo Echeverria Lozano, Purdue’s freshman kicker, has made 15-for-16 field goal attempts with a long of 48, which means all of his kicks have been made from inside roughly the 32-yard line. Anything behind that mark and Purdue could struggle to score. Need a Big Game From Penn State’s Secondary Penn State’s third level has been exceptional this season. The secondary is third nationally in passing, allowing 141.3 yards per game. But Purdue has a talented air game (22nd in FBS; 280.7 yards per game) led by junior quarterback Ryan Browne. Browne ranks in the top 25 in passing with 1,822 yards. He also has 10 touchdowns, three interceptions and has completed 65.5% of his throws. Browne’s favorite target has been wide receiver Asaad Waseem, who has 38 catches for 588 yards but only one touchdown. Purdue hasn’t been afraid to spread the ball around, though, with seven receivers tallying over 100 yards. Conversely, none of Penn State’s corners have allowed 100 yards in coverage this season. item.description: Soccer star Payton Galuski work out at Afrim's Sports Park last month in Colonie. (Jim Franco/Times Union) Long before the state championships and college offers, Payton Galuski would sit for hours with a ball at the Middletown Soccer Fields in Waterford, waiting for a pickup game to start. "She used to just rot at the field," said Addyson Galuski, Payton's older sister by four years. "If my parents didn't tell her it was time to go home, she'd just stay there." That relentless devotion laid the foundation for a grueling routine years later. Now, at 16, soccer takes her roughly three hours from her Waterford home, several times a week. After winning two state titles with the Waterford-Halfmoon girls' soccer team, being named state player of the year, playing on the boys' team and becoming the first girl named to a boys' all-state team, Payton Galuski walked away from high school soccer. The Penn State commit wanted a harder test. So, she chose to sit out her junior season this fall to focus on her training with FC Stars of Massachusetts, an Elite Clubs National League team near Boston. She is preparing for the upcoming ECNL season, which opens in December, a college career and, she hopes, a future that includes a professional career and a place on the United States women's national team. She wakes up early, hits the gym at 5:30 a.m., heads to school by 7:50 and often doesn't return home until around 11:30 p.m. She eats and does her homework during the car rides to and from workouts with the FC Stars. "It's a lot of training, a lot of practices, over in Massachusetts," Galuski said. "But I think it's worth it." Galuski comes from an athletic family. Among the family of athletes are her father, Kory Galuski, who won a state title with the Waterford-Halfmoon boys' soccer team in 1994 and his cousin, Mark Galuski, who coaches football at La Salle Institute. Another cousin, Courtney Galuski, played softball and basketball at Cohoes, where she once tied the national record with 15 3-pointers in a game against Schalmont in 2008. Kory and his wife, Stephanie Galuski, would take Payton, Addyson and their younger sister, Alexis, now 13, to the nearby soccer fields, often bringing the family dog. Kory set out cones and organized drills. Before long, Addyson noticed her younger sister wanted to keep working longer than she did. "She would train more than me. She would train harder," said Addyson Galuski, who is now in her junior season at Hartwick. "She was not backing down no matter what." Payton Galuski joined the Albany Alleycats Soccer Club around the age of 9. Galuski and the other younger players watched as Hutton demonstrated difficult skills and worked on her game. The Memphis Grizzlies have improved to 5-0 on the season after blowing out the Portland Trail Blazers on Ja Morant’s first game against his old team. Up 23 points with two and a half minutes remaining, the Grizzlies were already in celebration mode on the bench. Big man Isaiah Stewart had an unusual way of celebrating, though, as he proceeded to slap his teammates hard on the chest . item.title: Troy Aikman and Joe Buck’s ‘Monday Night Football’ Clash Revealed: ‘Never Thought You’d Do It to Me’
item.description: X/@MLFootball A bitter dispute between longtime NFL broadcasting partners Troy Aikman and Joe Buck has spilled into the open, raising questions about whether the pair will remain together after this season. New details about their heated confrontation before an October 12 Monday Night Football game emerged, The Athletic reported on Friday, October 30. Sources familiar with the situation described an argument inside the broadcast booth at SoFi Stadium before the Buffalo Bills faced the Los Angeles Rams . As First for Sports exclusively reported on October 19, the tension stems partly from Buck’s decision to sign a six-year, $108 million contract extension earlier this year without informing the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback, whose five-year, $90 million deal expires after the season. “It’s the biggest betrayal anyone in the industry can remember,” a source told First for Sports . BDG/ZOJ/WENN/Newscom/The Mega Agency Per The Athletic’s report, sources said Buck, 57, confronted Aikman, 59, asking, “You are not going to [explicit] talk to me?” “I’m not the reason you don’t have a contract,” Buck said, per the report. Aikman fired back, “I just never thought you’d do it to me.” “They got rid of them because you were screaming at them,” Buck responded, referring to turnover among ESPN ‘s production staff, according to the outlet. ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA Aikman met with ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro before the October 12 game to discuss his future, per the report. However, ESPN has declined Aikman’s request for a raise comparable to Buck’s, according to The Athletic. Contract discussions are now on hold until after the Super Bowl. Aikman and veteran sportscaster Buck have worked together calling NFL games since 2002, first at Fox Sports before moving to ESPN in 2022, per the outlet. They are expected to call Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027. Fox Sports analyst Greg Olsen is considered a leading potential replacement if Aikman leaves ESPN, according to the report. Aikman admitted there was a “50-50 chance” he would return to television next year during an October 28 event in Dallas, per an X post by sportswriter Tim Cowlishaw . item.title: Are Liverpool in a title challenge? Andoni Iraola reveals stance before Arsenal test
item.description: Andoni Iraola says it would still be too early to say whether Liverpool are in a Premier League title challenge – even if his side beat champions Arsenal on Sunday. The Reds are enjoying their best run under Iraola, winning four games in a row before progressing past Chelsea in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup in midweek. Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool could move three points behind Arsenal with a win at Anfield (Reuters) Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said the Reds could emerge as Arsenal’s closest challengers due to the uncertainty surrounding Manchester City this season, a feeling that could become stronger should they win against the champions and move three points behind Mikel Arteta’s team. "It's good if the fans have expectations and think we can win. But if you ask me, it is still very early in the season,” Iraola said. “I said before, it's still October, take one game at a time and I always say the first reference is normally when we have played against each other once, halfway through the season, and then you can start looking at the standings. “Now we are in a position where we need to improve, keep getting better.” There is a chance Szoboszlai is available for Liverpool (Getty) Liverpool, meanwhile, could be boosted by the return of Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz. Szoboszlai’s return form injury against Brentford two weeks ago lasted only 31 minutes but there is a chance the midfielder, who scored a stunning free-kick in Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Arsenal last season, is available. “We still have two days,” Iraola said. “I think they have a chance, yes."

item.title: Chelsea vs Manchester United: Alonso urges his side to learn from a tough week
item.description: Chelsea vs Manchester United: Alonso urges his side to learn from a tough week Xabi Alonso has called on Chelsea to learn from the tough moments as his side look to return to winning ways. Chelsea face Manchester United in the Premier League tomorrow lunchtime, seeking to bounce back from a challenging week. Alonso's side lost to Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge last weekend, before exiting the Carabao Cup at Liverpool in midweek. Chelsea lost the fourth-round tie on penalties after a 1-1 draw at Anfield. Alonso has urged his team to regroup, ahead of the visit of Manchester United. United arrive in West London under pressure after eight games without a win in all competitions. Ahead of the fixture, Alonso said his developing side will endure 'tough moments' but outlined the importance to learn from their setbacks. "We are back in Premier League mode and that for me is the main competition for us - this year and almost every year," the Spaniard said at his pre-match press conference. "It is a big one. We didn't have long to prepare but it's really important after the last home game we had that we keep winning games and get that winning feeling. "As soon as we left Liverpool, we were thinking about United. I saw a better version of us on Wednesday than I did on Saturday, even though the result wasn't what we wanted in either. This is a journey where we will have tough moments and we need to learn from them." Alonso confirmed that Maxence Lacroix will miss the clash with Manchester United, after sustaining a hamstring injury in midweek. The French defender will not return before the international break. Jorell Hato has also been ruled out. "Max picked up an injury and we expect he will not be available before the international break. He will be out for a few weeks."

item.title: Watch: Dani Olmo receives special commemorative shirt to celebrate 100 Barcelona appearances
item.description: Watch: Dani Olmo receives special commemorative shirt to celebrate 100 Barcelona appearances Last week turned out to be a bittersweet one for Barcelona midfielder Dani Olmo. Starting in the UEFA Champions League clash against Paris Saint-Germain, the midfielder made his 100th appearance for the club, reaching a major milestone. However, the night in Paris ended in major disappointment for the Spanish international as he suffered an adductor injury that will keep him out for four weeks . To pile on his misery, Barcelona suffered a 4-2 defeat on the night, tasting their first loss of the 2026/27 season. Dani Olmo receives commemorative shirt With little time between the game against PSG and the Clasico against Real Madrid, which the team lost as well, there was not much of an opportunity for Barcelona to celebrate Olmo’s special landmark. Earlier today, though, the Catalan giants recognised the achievement by presenting Olmo with a special shirt in a ceremony with the full squad after the training session. The 2026 FIFA World Cup winner posed for a picture with his teammates who congratulated him on reaching the milestone with the Blaugrana . Two years, five trophies Olmo left Barcelona’s La Masia youth academy at a young age to join Dinamo Zagreb. He returned to the club a decade later in 2024, with the Catalans signing him from RB Leipzig. The Spaniard’s time back at his boyhood club has been far from straightforward – from early registration issues to constant injury problems, the road has not been easy. Olmo suffered an injury against PSG. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) But through all of that, Olmo has now made 100 appearances for Barcelona, in which he has scored 21 goals and registered 19 assists. During his time with the Blaugrana , the 28-year-old midfielder has won as many as five trophies: two La Liga titles, two Spanish Super Cups, and one Copa del Rey. Even though he has had to battle it out with Fermin Lopez for a starting berth, Olmo remains a key part of the plans for Hansi Flick thanks to his technical ability and versatile nature. For now, the Spanish international’s full focus will be on making a swift recovery from his injury so that he can return to playing for Barcelona.

item.description: Miami Dolphins rookie left guard Kadyn Proctor is unlikely to play in Week 8 home game against the New England Patriots , due to a concussion, coach Jeff Hafley said. "Not looking very good," Hafley said. Proctor experienced symptoms this week. Proctor did hold a Monday press conference with local reporters. Jarrett Kingston has been next in line. Kingston played pretty well when replacing Jonah Savaiinaea in a recent game. The offensive line has been the strongest part of Miami's game in a 1-5 start. Proctor has been excellent and has not allowed a sack. Miami has topped 100 rushing yards in five consecutive games. Miami signed guard Christian Haynes after he was waived by the Seahawks this week. Dolphins cornerback JuJu Brents, unlike Proctor, did some practice in the week leading up to the Patriots game. There is some progress and if Brents is cleared, he'll play, according to coach Hafley. item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have officially suspended Dylan Larkin without pay, and interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said Larkin has informed the team he will no longer play for Detroit. One of the 10 teams on Larkin’s approved trade list is the Dallas Stars, and Pierre LeBrun told TSN on Thursday that the list has not been expanded. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dallas Stars Need to Sign Jason Robertson Before Any Dylan Larkin Trade Jason Robertson is being paid $12 million this season on the one-year contract he signed in July to avoid arbitration, a deal that sends him to unrestricted free agency next summer. He is 27 years old and should be Dallas’s number one priority before trading for Larkin. The Stars cannot sign him to an extension until Jan. 1. Pierre LeBrun of The Athletic wrote in his team-by-team look at Larkin’s market, “I don’t believe that the Stars have been involved or feel they can be a player in this. They’ve got Jason Robertson and his future to figure out first.” This would be the right approach for the Stars organization. It would be a little silly for them to trade for Larkin now instead of waiting until January to sign Robertson. If he is signed in January to a long-term deal and if Larkin is not traded yet, then by all means Dallas should make a move for him then. Dallas is not the only name on the list that is sitting still, either. TSN’s Chris Johnston said a number of the 10 teams are not in active talks with Detroit right now, and that the Minnesota Wild are believed to have the strongest offer on the table, with two roster players and multiple first-round picks. Jason Robertson’s Numbers Show Why He Comes First Robertson has played in 13 games this season for the Stars. He has scored five goals and recorded eight assists for 13 points, with a plus-5 rating, according to NHL.com . Robertson is very important for the future of the Stars. There is a chance that he could get a big payday from Dallas.

item.description: Photo by Erica Denhoff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Panthers took an ugly 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday Night Football, and Carolina responded to that loss by parting ways with defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. Todd Wash was named interim defensive coordinator and will call the defensive plays, according to a release from the Panthers shared by Joe Person of The Athletic. Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive pass game coordinator Ejiro Evero. DL line coach Todd Wash named interim DC. pic.twitter.com/7zFf3cZeYj — Joe Person (@josephperson) October 30, 2026 Ejiro was hired by the Panthers as the team’s defensive coordinator in 2023 after one season in the DC role with the Los Angeles Rams. He was hired during Frank Reich’s tenure as the Panthers’ head coach, but Dave Canales retained him when he was hired by Carolina. Wash spent five seasons as the Jaguars’ defensive coordinator. From the Panthers’ release : Wash originally joined Carolina’s staff in 2023 and has 31 years of coaching experience, including 20 in the NFL. He spent five seasons (2016-20) serving as the defensive coordinator for the Jacksonville Jaguars, including in 2017 when the team had the second-ranked defense in the league and advanced to the AFC Championship Game. It wasn’t just Thursday night’s loss that led to the decision. The loss to the Packers on a short week came on the heels of an embarrassing 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers in Week 7. But Baker Mayfield only threw for about 63 yards, and the Buccaneers ran all over Carolina. On Thursday night, the Panthers let Jordan Love throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns while Bryce Young took six sacks and finished with a QBR of 36.2. In addition to the termination of Evero and Cooley, the Panthers announced that OLB/run game specialist AC Carter will also take on defensive line coaching responsibilities. Secondary coach Renardo Hill will retain his position. The Panthers are sitting at 3-4 and remain in first place in a very weird NFC South, but if the Falcons win this week, that will change. item.title: The Biggest Takeaways From Stockton Kings Media Day
item.description: The Stockton Kings have reached the NBA G League Finals two years in a row, with one trip culminating in their first championship. Their roster has seen tremendous turnover, with only one player returning from last season. The team features plenty of new faces, from two-way players with Sacramento to trade acquisitions. Stockton has a winning culture. Despite the Sacramento Kings reaching the NBA Playoffs once over the last twenty years, the Stockton Kings rarely miss the G League Playoffs. Landing so many new players may lead some to believe the team is looking to take on a new identity. That’s not entirely the case, as many players cite defensive intensity and pace, two hallmarks of the squad’s previous system, as points consistently preached. Nearly every player touched upon fighting to reach the pinnacle of G League success, the Finals. They hope to continue the winning legacy the organization has built. “We’re looking forward to building on last season,” Head Coach Will Scott said . Every Player Knows Their Role and Is Ready to Build On It Every member of the Stockton Kings is ready and willing to integrate themselves within the system. That starts with playing with intensity and energy. One of their premier players is former Toronto Raptor Jonathan Mogbo . Mogbo has played in three games with Stockton’s NBA affiliate, and he made his presence felt. When asked how he maintains such a high level of physicality during his minutes, he said , “that’s my job.” Mogbo understands his role and embraces it. The Stockton staff also want their guys to play with freedom, while growing their skills. item.title: Troy Aikman sparred with ESPN chairman right before explosive Joe Buck MNF argument
item.description: Matthew Emmons-USA TODAY Sports. Troy Aikman sparred with ESPN chairman right before explosive Joe Buck MNF argument appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Even more details have emerged about Troy Aikman and Joe Buck ’s fight before Monday Night Football (MNF) a couple of weeks ago, including that the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback got into it with the chairman of ESPN. The Athletic reports that before Aikman and Buck’s blow-up argument, the Super Bowl-winning quarterback “had a tense one-hour chat” with Jimmy Pitaro, ESPN ’s chairman. They reportedly discussed Aikman’s strained relationship with Buck and their future as a duo. The former quarterback was frustrated with Buck, who signed a five-year contract extension with the network. Pitaro put all his cards on the table, asking him, “Could you still work with Joe?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Aikman claimed that he could, but this was still a prelude to his fight with Buck. The Athletic believes “it is clear ESPN has taken Buck’s side in the pending divorce.” The tension has been building for years. Sources told The Athletic that there was “off-air unease” for the first five weeks of the year. It might have boiled over after Buck signed his new deal. Buck reportedly believes that Aikman made “situations untenable for the production staff” ( Monday Night Football has been through five producers and directors since their arrival four years ago) by “barking orders for replays he desired.” However, Aikman believes Buck is “a master of manipulating to get what he wants.” The fight before the Monday Night Football game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Buffalo Bills started with Buck confronting Aikman, asking, ‘You are not going to f**king talk to me?” Apparently, Aikman felt like Buck initiated the fight “to force a public backlash to appear as the good guy.” During the argument, Buck twisted the knife by saying, “I’m not the reason you don’t have a contract.” The Cowboys legend reportedly believes Buck is the reason for the producer and director turnover during their time at ESPN, and he felt he was next. He said, “I just never thought you’d do it to me,” in response to Buck’s remark. This prompted the NFL and MLB announcer to say, “They got rid of them because you were screaming at them.” While Buck got his extension first, ESPN was interested in bringing Aikman back. His team reportedly used Tom Brady’s $37.5 million salary at FOX as a benchmark. They were negotiating a $30 million salary for Aikman. ESPN then said it would be pausing negotiations until after the Super Bowl. Still, his team said he’d return for a similar 18% pay bump like Buck’s deal, but ESPN declined. We’ll see what happens. Aikman appears ready to leave the network . When asked about it, he didn’t go into details but said he’ll “be a free agent at the end of the year” and was open to seeing what other opportunities arise. Related: Patriots vs. Dolphins
